The cure — a ConnAck-driven supervisor that re-subscribes, re-asserts availability, and republishes discovery on every connect — ships on the pinned rumqttc 0.24.0 with zero dependency churn, and is the same disease the incumbent Windows agent fixed in a patch release [[releases-hass-agenthassagent-github]].

The comment is false: sysfs attributes default to `root:root 0644`, so 0664 grants group-write to group *root*, and io's only group anywhere is `wheel` (`common.nix:139` — no host adds io to `video`) [[interim-report-fleet-service-model-by-host-class]].

**The backends the fleet never runs.** The audit closes on the three crates no host exercises: backend-kde hard-fails without a session bus (`Connection::session().await?` at `backend-kde/src/lib.rs:41`) and has zero fleet consumers because no jupiterOS host runs Plasma — greps for plasma/kde across hosts and modules return nothing, and the hard-fail is the stated boundary condition for ever hosting a desktop class (it must adopt the generic backend's warn-and-continue degradation first); backend-gamescope's only fleet consumer is callisto's arcade session, with kiosks reaching gamescope via the shared dashboard-gaming modeSpecs; backend-lutris ships behind the `jupiter.gaming.console` appCatalog but no host configuration exercises its launch-only buttons, its JSON field names hedged unverified — gamescope and lutris both among the backends the repo itself flags "Unverified in a live environment" [[interim-report-fleet-service-model-by-host-class]] [[repo-map-ha-linux-agent]] [[interim-report-adopt-vs-build-honest-verdict]].

**The quality gates are absent, not merely failing.** Eight test functions exist — three in `discovery.rs`, five in `backend-launcher`, all pure shape guards, zero on any hardware, D-Bus (Linux's inter-process message bus), or MQTT path — but the flake's (the repo's Nix build definition) checks hold only a build and clippy (Rust's linter) with `--deny warnings`: no test hook exists, so zero of the eight ever run in any gate [[interim-report-testing-gate-for-hardware-daemon]].

A dead `tls` knob sits at `config.rs:88`, the README has drifted (backend-hardware undocumented; zfs, syncthing, and lutris flagged by the repo itself as "Unverified in a live environment"), and the hardware backend exposes placeholder select options rather than sysfs-enumerated values [[interim-report-adopt-vs-build-honest-verdict]].

**The fleet coverage fact.** The agent runs on four of seven hosts — the TCxWave kiosks (amalthea, adrastea, metis, thebe) — while callisto deliberately opts out (its arcade-console config strips the wiring), europa runs nothing despite the zfs/syncthing/headscale backends existing for exactly that host, and pallene — a ZFS-less Kamatera VPS whose own header reads "No ZFS, no impermanence, no sops-nix, no ha-linux-agent" — hard-opts-out [[interim-report-adopt-vs-build-honest-verdict]] [[interim-report-headless-privilege-ladder]]. The defect distribution is the strategic fact: failures cluster in the lifecycle core every host class shares — `agent.rs` and config plumbing — while the per-backend surfaces are small, self-contained crates of 100–330 lines behind two traits [[interim-report-adopt-vs-build-honest-verdict]].

rumqttc's poll loop reconnects unconditionally — "Continuing to poll will reconnect to the broker if there is a disconnection" — and advertises "Automatic reconnections by just continuing the eventloop.poll()/connection.iter() loop", re-subscription conspicuously absent [[eventloop-in-rumqttc-rust]] [[rumqttc-rust]].

Issue #250, open since February 2021 and still labelled in-pipeline, documents the footgun: after a clean-session reconnect, "I'm not seeing any data coming in from subscribed topics", because subscriptions live only in broker-side session state [[automatic-reconnect-and-subscribed-topics-issue-250-bytebeamiorumqtt-github]].

The in-pipeline fix, PR #1052, is open, unreviewed, v5-scoped, and only emits a reconnect *signal* — its own caller pattern re-subscribes in application code, so subscription ownership stays with the application even if it merges [[interim-report-rumqttc-dependency-fitness]].

And the pinned version offers no alternative hook: 0.24.0's `Event` enum has exactly two variants — `Incoming` and `Outgoing`, no `Reconnect` — so `poll()` yielding `Packet::ConnAck` on every connect is the only reconnect signal the pinned version has, making the raw ConnAck match not a workaround but the mandatory design [[interim-report-rumqttc-dependency-fitness]].

Paho, the alternative, exposes rich reconnect callbacks but leaves re-subscription application-owned too, and drags a C toolchain onto every NixOS fleet build — default builds need CMake, a C compiler, and system OpenSSL, a foreign dependency chain in every host closure (the interim's one open question, whether nixpkgs' paho-c packaging is already clean, is unverified; the application-owned re-subscription point alone decides the client question) [[asyncclient-in-paho_mqttasync_client-rust]] [[github-eclipse-pahopahomqttrust-pahomqttrust-github]] [[interim-report-rumqttc-dependency-fitness]].

The queue mechanics are per-client: mosquitto counts each client's queued messages against `max_queued_messages` (default 1000), and for a disconnected client the in-flight adjustment zeroes, freeing the full queue depth for offline replay [[databasec]].

The request-channel capacity of 64 at `agent.rs:62` contradicts rumqttc's recommendation to set capacity 0 when managing pending state — during an outage, up to 64 stale messages queue and replay as a burst [[rumqttrumqttcsrceventlooprs-at-main-bytebeamiorumqtt-github]].

Worse is starvation: `backend-syncthing` builds its reqwest client with no timeout (reqwest has none by default), and `Agent::run` polls all backends sequentially in one task, so one hung syncthing daemon freezes every sensor while availability still reads "online" — sensors that lie rather than sensors that vanish, the worst failure class a fleet can carry [[interim-report-mqtt-lifecycle-supervisor-spec]].

On every `ConnAck` — first connect or reconnect, either `session_present` — re-issue all command-topic subscribes (idempotent; subscribe-before-connect is safe because requests buffer in the bounded channel until post-ConnAck) and re-assert retained "online" [[rumqttrumqttcsrceventlooprs-at-main-bytebeamiorumqtt-github]].

First, `clean_session = true` (explicit, stable client id) against the persistent-session instinct: a persistent session's only unique deliverable here is broker-side queueing of QoS 1 commands for an offline agent, and the kiosks power off overnight — a week-old launcher toggle or reboot replaying as fresh on Monday boot, with no TTL in v3.1.1 (issue #211, open and stale since December 2020) and no payload timestamp to age it by, is a hazard no source states directly but the overnight-off pattern and rumqtt's documented lack of any pending-message TTL jointly imply [[rumqttc-reconnection-to-mqtt-broker-and-pending-messages-ttl-issue-211-bytebeami]].

Second, a premise correction that strengthens the design: 0.24.0 is *not* v3.1.1-locked — `src/lib.rs:113` declares `pub mod v5;` with full property support inside the pinned version, and the module is not a stubbed half-implementation: its single `unimplemented!()` sits on request variants (PubComp/SubAck/UnsubAck/PingResp) the public client never sends — unreachable from agent code — so message and session expiry are a module switch away, a named future option rather than the reason for any workaround [[interim-report-rumqttc-dependency-fitness]].

The 0.25.1 upgrade was actually run — check, test, clippy all exit 0, zero code changes — and reverted, because it buys nothing the supervisor needs; the identical public API across the two versions is itself evidence the bump is cosmetic [[interim-report-rumqttc-dependency-fitness]].

The packaging counter first. "One custom module away" carries a heavy deployment cost on this fleet: lnxlink is not in nixpkgs at all — an individual hit a wall packaging it in October 2025 and no one has upstreamed a service module in the year since an unmerged draft appeared in August 2024 — and its Python dependency surface (pygobject3, ewmh, xlib, opencv-python, pulsectl, pyalsaaudio, docker, speechrecognition in one propagated list) is the ongoing per-release maintenance cost for whoever owns that packaging [[python-packaging-error-needs-specific-setuptools-version-nixos-discourse]].

No module precedent exists for that class: lnxlink modules are hand-written per host, not generated from fleet configuration [[lnxlink]]. go-hass-agent is packaged as a *binary* but has no NixOS service module: a full-text pass over module-list.nix returns zero occurrences of either incumbent, while the home-automation directory hosts home-assistant, esphome, zigbee2mqtt, zwave-js, matter-server, govee2mqtt, evcc, ebusd, and homebridge [[module-listnix]].
